column1: # Declared exceptions to the shaped patterns in hygiene-patterns.tsv.
# Format: label<TAB>extended-regex, in the SAME dialect the pattern it
# exempts is written in -- POSIX ERE, because `hygiene.sh` applies this
# through `sed -E`, the one tool that shares grep -E's regex flavour, so a
# maintainer reading a pattern and its exception beside it reads one syntax
# rather than two.
# WHAT THIS DOES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. An exception does not loosen or
# rewrite the pattern it names: `hygiene.sh` still runs the pattern's own
# regex, unedited, against the full line. Every occurrence of the exception
# regex is then removed from that line, and the pattern is asked again
# whether anything is LEFT. If nothing is, every hit on the line was
# accounted for by a declared-safe form and the line is clean; if something
# still matches, it is reported exactly as before -- so a line carrying both
# a forge remote AND a private one still fires.
# This is a data-driven carve-out, not a weaker pattern: the shape the
# pattern names is unchanged, and a form not listed here still fires -- a
# login at a DOTTED private host, colon-terminated, is the whole reason
# `ssh-user-at-host` keeps matching after this file exists. (Not a bare,
# dotless hostname: a fresh-instance review of #83 found an earlier example
# here used one and never fired, since the pattern requires a dot --
# pre-existing and unrelated to this file, corrected rather than repeated.
# Not written as a literal instance again, for the same reason this row's
# own regex is not written as the string it exempts.)
# Ruled 2026-09-12 on #72. `ssh-user-at-host` exists to catch a PRIVATE
# remote a captured log carries by accident -- a build box, a personal
# machine -- and a public forge's own SSH remote form is not that: it is the
# same string in every clone of every public repository on that host,
# published by the forge itself. Four forges named here; the shape is one
# alternation, so a fifth is one more name in it, not a new row.
# AND A PACKAGE LOCKFILE'S OWN KEY FORM, by the same argument. pnpm spells a
# resolved package as `name@1.2.3:` (and `name@1.2.3(peer@4.5.6)` inside a
# peer suffix), which the pattern reads as a login at a dotted host. A dotted
# all-numeric "host" with exactly three parts -- optionally a pre-release of
# one word and one number, `-beta.2` -- terminated by `:`, `(`, `)` or `'`,
# is a semver in a lockfile and is not a hostname at all -- it is the
# same string in every install from the same registry. The terminator is
# part of the exception on purpose: an IPv4 has a fourth part after its third
# dot, so a login at a private address is left exactly as it was and still
# fires. (No literal instance of either form is written here, per the rule
# above.)
# Added 2026-09-20 with the first JavaScript package (`exercise/`); disclosed
# on that PR as an edit outside its directory.
ssh-user-at-host
# AND A PYTHON REQUIREMENTS PIN, by the same argument as the lockfile key form. `pip freeze` (and `uv pip freeze`)
# spells a pinned package as `name==1.2.3.4`, and a four-part version that opens with 10 reads to `private-ipv4` as a
# private address (a CUDA library's pin in `rtx6000ada-host`'s frozen package set, #143). The exempt form is a
# whole line that is a pin and nothing else: a package name, `==`, a four-part version, end of line, as `pip freeze`
# writes it. An address anywhere else -- a URL, a host field, a bare line, or after `==` with anything else on the line
# -- still fires. The scanner hands this file grep's `path:line:content`, so the pattern anchors on that prefix (path,

# line number) and the package name follows it directly, and the history check scans patches, so a leading `+` or `-` is allowed there. (A line that is nothing but `name==10.x.x.x` is exempt whatever the name says; that is the cost of
# reading lines, not files.)
# AND A LLAMA.CPP LOG LINE'S ELAPSED-TIME PREFIX (#335, ruled 5984747931). llama.cpp opens every log line with the time
# since start as minutes, seconds, milliseconds and microseconds, dotted, then a space, a level letter and the source
# that logged it. From minute 10 on, that prefix reads to `private-ipv4` as a private address (a server log of #335's
# arm C, past ten minutes). The exempt form is that prefix and its suffix only, at the start of the scanned line:
# `10`, then exactly 2, 3 and 3 digits, a space, a level letter (I, W, E or D), a space, and one listed source
# (`slot`, `srv`, `Final`, `kl_divergence`, `perplexity`) followed by a space or a colon. The list is the sources the
# committed llama.cpp logs under substrates/ print after loading, by a literal grep (#419's review): `srv` as late as
# minute 27, `Final` (the perplexity and KLD tools' last line) 21, `slot` 14, `kl_divergence` and `perplexity` 3.
# Every other source in those logs prints only in minute 0 or 1, while loading, and is not listed.
# Only the prefix is removed, so an address anywhere else on the line still fires, and so does one at the start of a
# line without that suffix. The cost, disclosed: an address whose last three parts are exactly 2, 3 and 3 digits,
# at the start of a line, followed by exactly that suffix, would pass; no server writes that. hygiene.sh reads one
# row per label, so this form is a second alternative of the requirements-pin row, which is kept verbatim before it.
# (Minutes 172 and 192 would read as the other private ranges; no committed log runs that long, and this row does
# not cover them.)
private-ipv4
